text: Standard invoices usually bill real catalog items that already have their own descriptions and accounting. Debit memos, on-account credits, and chargebacks don't have that luxury, somebody needs to describe what a charge is for, on the spot. Memo lines solve that with a reusable, predefined description and default accounting.

A standard memo line is a predefined description, restocking fee, freight correction, service call charge, paired with default accounting and optionally a default price. Instead of typing free text and picking a GL account from scratch, the person entering a debit memo or credit just selects the memo line.

Here's what it actually defaults. The standardized wording that prints on the transaction. Accounting references that feed AutoAccounting, so the same charge always posts to the same place no matter who enters it. A tax classification. And optionally a fixed unit price for flat fees.

Picture a damaged shipment from Northwind Fixtures Co to Harborline Retail Group, with a seventy-five dollar restocking fee charged for the replacement. The AR clerk selects the Restocking Fee memo line on a debit memo instead of typing it in from scratch. It fills the standardized description, defaults the usual GL account through AutoAccounting, and applies the right tax classification automatically, the same way every restocking fee gets coded company-wide.
